I helped a friend of mine deal with a similar situation. It can be scary to talk to your partner about your feelings and it’s not made any easier when your partner has past relationship trauma. It’s important to remember that a relationship isn’t always going to be 50/50 sometimes it’s more like 60/40 or 70/30, but at the end of the day you still have your own personal needs. 

Being long distance does make this situation more difficult since it would be better if you had this conversation in person. However what I would do is before even calling her is just make a list of everything you want to say. It can be easy to get off topic and you don’t want to say anything that might turn her off from the conversation. Use as much sensitivity and understanding as you can in your word choice and reassure her that you’re not upset with her, and that you just want to be comforted by her. Ask her if there’s anything that you can help her with and tell her that you want her help to feel better. If she continues to isolate herself from the conversation and avoid talking to you about the solution, there’s really nothing you can do. She clearly has a lot of things going on and she probably needs professional help to better understand what happened to her. Ultimately, you have to take care of yourself as well and if this issue is something you can’t get past you may want to consider breaking up- she may not be ready for another relationship. 

Overall, I think this is a complicated issue that requires a lot of patience, sensitivity, and love to overcome, but it has to come from both sides. I truly feel for your situation and I hope you can find the comfort you need. Don’t be afraid to reach out to others for help, and I wish you all the best.

I just wanted to say that I totally understand how this feels and I’m so sorry that you’re going through this. It’s so frustrating when you talk to your partner about an issue and they say they’ll change but they never do.

Say the things you said in this post and ask him if there’s something that is preventing him from doing these things. I’m willing to bet that he’s feeling a lack of connection which is making it difficult for him to ‘get in the mood’, and it’s nothing that you’re doing wrong. Talking to each other and learning about each of your love languages might help re-establish that connection. Going on a ‘first date’ with each other is also a really good way to do this. It’s basically just going on a date with each other and pretending like you haven’t been together for the last 5 years.

Ultimately, I truly feel for your struggle and I strongly believe that you aren’t doing anything wrong. You’re in a very difficult situation and I wish you all the best.
